title: Puppet Knight - Element Impact && Element Icons

posts.author: Puppet Knight
posts.body:
This plugin introduces dynamic elemental mechanics, allowing you to inflict states, modify damage based on target conditions, and scale power with consecutive uses or hits of elements.
Key Features:
Custom Element Cycles
:
Define relationships between elements, including strengths and weaknesses.
Support for single-element cycles (where elements are strong against themselves) and two-element cycles (where elements are strong against each other).
Multi-element cycles for traditional rock-paper-scissors-style interactions.
Dynamic Element Rules
:
Choose how battlers' current elements are determined with three flexible options:
Last Used Element
: Based on the last skill's element.
Last Hit Element
: Based on the last element the battler was hit by.
Higher Stack
: Prioritizes the element with the higher consecutive usage or hit count.
Stack-Based Adjustments
:
Track consecutive uses (Use Stacks) and hits (Hit Stacks) of elements.
Apply scaling damage modifiers based on stack counts, allowing for dynamic damage interactions.
State Impact Effects
:
Inflict or remove states based on elements, with configurable chances.
Add damage modifiers for specific state and element combinations.
Reflect Damage Mechanic
:
Option to reflect damage back to the user if specific element based conditions are met by the target
Debug Mode
:
Easily toggle detailed console logging to debug and fine-tune your configurations.
Script Calls:
assign icons to element ids, also more easily search element ids and names based on skill id
Highly Configurable
:
Define multipliers (percentage-based) for strengths, weaknesses, and stack effects.
Flexible parameter settings to adjust maximum stacks, element relationships, and more.
Use Cases
:
Create engaging rock-paper-scissors-style elemental battles.
Add layers of strategy with dynamic stack-based damage scaling.
Reward players for mastering elemental mechanics in your game.
The plugin can be found on itch!
Puppet Knight - Element Impact & Element Icons by Puppet Knight

posts.body:
Big Big update!
Absorbed some amazing feedback from casper to update how a lot of the multipliers work, but mainly to remove IIFE from the plugin. This allows me to allow fellow devs more flexibility in utilizing the parts of the plugin they want in more modular ways.
Full Version 1.1 update details below:
1. Introduction of Element Cycles
​
Brand New Feature
:
Define relationships between elements in
Element Cycles
, supporting:
Single-Element Cycles
: An element can be strong against itself, applying the Strength Multiplier.
Two-Element Cycles
: Both elements are strong against each other, consistently applying the Strength Multiplier.
Multi-Element Cycles
: Cyclical strength and weakness relationships (e.g., rock-paper-scissors mechanics).
Fully customizable via plugin parameters, including configurable Strength Multiplier and Weakness Multiplier.
2. Complete Code Overhaul
​
Refactored to enable
reusability of functions
outside the plugin's default flow:
PK_ElementImpact.getCurrentElement: Dynamically determines a battler's current element based on the
Element Rule
.
PK_ElementImpact.getElementMultiplier: Provides a flexible, standalone method to calculate the damage multiplier based on element relationships.
Simplified and modularized logic for better extensibility and compatibility with other plugins or custom systems.
3. New Element Rule Parameter
​
Added the
Element Rule
parameter to control how a battler's element is determined:
Last Used Element
: Uses the last element applied by the battler.
Last Hit Element
: Uses the last element that hit the battler.
Higher Stack
: Selects the element associated with the higher stack between consecutive uses and hits.
4. Improved Damage Calculation Workflow
​
Reorganized the damage calculation process to ensure accuracy:
Elements for the
user
and
target
are captured before updates to lastUsedElem and lastHitElem.
Stacks (lastUsedStack and lastHitStack) now contribute consistently to damage scaling.
The
Element Cycle Multiplier
applies after all other calculations, ensuring it reflects the correct relationships and rules.
5. Debugging Enhancements
​
Introduced a
Debug Mode
plugin parameter:
Enables detailed logging for easy debugging of elements, stacks, and multipliers.
Optional and configurable via plugin parameters.
Summary
​
This version introduces a major leap in functionality with the
Element Cycles
system, offering powerful new mechanics for elemental interactions. The code has been overhauled to improve modularity and enable reusability, making it easier to integrate and extend the plugin. These updates provide developers with more flexibility, precision, and control over elemental mechanics in their projects.
updated plugin can be found on itch!

posts.author: Puppet Knight
posts.body:
Version 1.2 Update!
Added in a Reflect Mechanic option. This will allow targets to reflect skill damage back to the user of an action when specific element and stack conditions are met. This relies on the `Element Rule` established in
1.1
.
New Notetags:
<noReflect> This notetag is used to prevent a skill from being reflected no matter what the targets element is
<noStacks> This notetag is used to avoid damage changes or reductions based on stacks. Element cycle changes still Apply
<noCycle> This notetag is used to avoid damage changes due to Element Cycles
<ignoreAll> This notetag is used for all three effects above
None of these notetags mitigate damage related to state Impact multipliers. Stack increases and element changes still update as needed.
On deck feature:
I am planning to create an additional notetag that will allow skills to reverse the element cycle they fall under (think the "Reaver" weapons like
https://fireemblem.fandom.com/wiki/Lancereaver
in Fire Emblem), but purely for elements. I just want to be sure it respects the multiplier correctly as well as test how it would interact with reflections if at all.
Any suggestions/asks for new features on this plugin? Don't hesitate to give me a shout. I'm trying to hit as many things that don't seem possible out of the box for MZ when it comes to Elements.

posts.author: Puppet Knight
posts.body:
Version 1.3 Update
Feature Update:
Added in the aforementioned notetag to reverse element cycle damage
<reverseCycle>
Any skill utilizing this notetag will reverse the cycle of the element its utilizing, if that element belongs to a cycle.
For Example, if the cycle is set up as Fire > Air > Water > Fire (Strength Multiplier x150%, Weakness Multiplier 50%)
Normally, a Fire skill hitting an enemy whose current element is Water would have its damage reduced by 50%
However if a fire skill with the notetag
<reverseCycle>
hits a water target, the strength multiplier would apply instead.
Bug Fix:
While testing reverseCycle I noticed the timing of when elementCurrent and the lastHit/Used properties was a bit funky. I cleaned up the order a bit to make sure anytime a battlers elementCurrent is being checked using the function `PK_ElementImpact.getCurrentElement`, it will be accurate.
Next Steps:
Though I'm likely going to take a step away from plugin building to focus on my project, I do have some things in mind I want to do here still.
Namely working on some Item Notetags to allow specific element effects, as well as some extra skill notetags to do things like maximize the users stacks.
There is also a bit of tweaking I want to do still to how stacks and elementCurrent are reset, and ways to avoid the stack being disrupted. This could look like a plugin parameter where it looks at the type of damage a skill does (like only HP or MP damage types affect elementCurrent and stacks), or something more tedious for the dev like a notetag. But we'll see. A lot of the answers generally come from the direction my game's going and then I code the solution in.
As always let me know if there's anything you like to see. Next to EquipSlotsChange, this has been a fun plugin for me to work on and want to do a lot more with it as a Elements and States solution.

Version 1.4 Update
NEW SCRIPT CALLS + Standalone "Lite" plugin
I've added in a new parameter structure that allows devs/users to associate Icons with element ids. This will make drawing specific elements in your project a little easier. Gone are the days of tracking down everywhere you tried to draw "Fire" as icon 47, when really you wanna use 200!!
also added two more functions to easily search element ids and names based on skill id
ElementImpact contains all the functionality of the standalone plugin "ElementIcon". So no need to have both if you're using the core plugin already. I will be updating ElementImpact further to integrate the new script calls soon, but for now, they act fairly independently.

Obviously the route we were discussing previously would certainly be a better fix, but for now i devised something that works good enough:
Make a state for each element:
Name: the element
Icon: the element icon you set
Remove at battle end
Auto removal timing: action end 2-2 (it disappears instantly if it's 1-1)
Then for each elemental skill, before any damage calculations, add
a.addState(X);                   where X is the ID of the corresponding element state.
Then once you use a skill, the element icon will display for that character until their next action, which will create a new one.
only 2 caveats:
1. I'm using a customized UI so i forgot what was in the normal one. if the RTP HUD displays states, then no problem, but if it doesn't you'll need a plugin
2.  This will obviously only work if you're using the "last used" element style. if you're using the last hit style, something i haven;t tested but may be worth a shot is doing the same thing but making enemy attacks apply that element state instead of applying it to self with the formula box, but don't be surprised if it doesn't work. i genuinely cannot think of anything that could work for most stack style

I have added some compatibility with NUUN_MultiElement to automatically check return information on additional elements when they are present via  the  notetag `<multElement:>`
